explanation: Recursively permute the prefix without its last character, then insert that removed character at every position of each smaller permutation. An ordered set removes duplicates.
correctness: Deleting one occurrence of the removed last character from any full permutation leaves a permutation of the remaining prefix. Recursion generates that smaller string, and reinserting at every position regenerates the full permutation. Every generated string has exactly the input multiplicities, while the set retains each distinct result once.
walkthrough: For input ac, recursively permute the prefix a, obtaining {a}. Inserting c before a yields ca; inserting it after a yields ac. The ordered set returns {ac,ca}.
edgeCases: repeated characters under the bank extension.
timeComplexity: O(n * n! * log(n! + 1)) worst-case character work for n distinct characters, including string copies and ordered-set comparisons; repeated characters can reduce the generated set.
spaceComplexity: O(n * n!) result and intermediate string storage in the distinct-character worst case, plus O(n) recursion depth.
